reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Colles Fracture Distal Radius: dinner fork deformity of wrist after slipping on ice and falling onto outstretched hand. 64F with osteopenia presenting with dorsally displaced, angulated extra-articular distal radius fracture with radial shortening on radiographs.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Colles Fracture Distal Radius.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Colles Fracture Distal Radius.
reference_soap.plan: Obtain wrist radiographs and urgently document skin integrity, distal pulses, capillary refill, sensation, and motor function. Immobilize, provide appropriate analgesia, and arrange reduction/casting or orthopedic management according to alignment and stability; repeat neurovascular checks after any manipulation or splinting. Escalate immediately for an open fracture, worsening pain/tight swelling, pale or cool fingers, or new numbness/weakness.

teaching.one_liner: 64F with osteopenia, fell on ice onto an outstretched hand, now with a dinner-fork wrist deformity.
red_flags: Neurovascular status of the hand must be checked

must_ask.say: Can you describe exactly how you fell and landed on your hand?
Does your wrist look bent or deformed to you?

must_ask.objective: Screen for finger numbness or color change
must_ask.say: Can you feel and move all your fingers normally, and are they a normal color?
Have you been diagnosed with weak bones or taken bone density medication?

must_ask.objective: Explain the reduction and casting plan
must_ask.say: We will first check circulation and nerve function and review the X-rays. If reduction is needed, it is done with appropriate pain control, followed by immobilization and repeat circulation and nerve checks; we should also arrange bone-health follow-up.
